chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from the one who mentioned it, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Muhammad ibn Marid, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A hadith has been reported to us that you said: When you recognize (the Wilayah), then do what you will.' He said, 'I have said that.' I said, 'And even if they commit adultery, or steal, or drink wine?' He said to me, 'We are to Allah and to Him we shall return. By Allah, they have not done us justice by saying that we would be seized by the deed while it is dropped from them. I only said: When you recognize (the Wilayah), then do what you will, from little good and much, for it will be accepted from you.'

key_terms.أُخِذْنَا بِالْعَمَلِ: We are seized/judged by the deed

ai.seo_question: What does the Imam mean by 'When you recognize, do what you will' in relation to good deeds and sins?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the theological debate regarding 'laxity' (Tafweed) by clarifying that 'recognition' (Ma' al-Qalb) serves as a spiritual key that guarantees the acceptance of all good deeds, regardless of their magnitude. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refutes the notion that believers are judged solely by major sins while disbelievers escape accountability, emphasizing that true Gnosis elevates even minor acts of worship. This context highlights the Shia emphasis on the transformative power of inner conviction over mere ritualistic compliance.
